reason: The source (OptionsPlaybook, a secondary educational site, not OCC itself) supports the first two parts: open interest is not updated intraday and OCC posts it the morning after. The backtest consequence is the drafter's inference. An Alpaca staff post (Feb 2026) says that after OCC's site posting, the figure is not distributed industry-wide until the next business morning, so on some vendor feeds day-1 OI only appears on day 3. Prior-day OI is therefore a best case, not a guarantee. theocc.com was not checked directly because it is blocked (403).
found: open interest is a lagging number: it's not updated during the course of a trading day. Instead, it is officially posted by The OCC the morning after any given trading session
suggested_fix: Option open interest is not updated intraday; OCC posts it the morning after each session (per OptionsPlaybook), so a backtest entering on day T can use at most day T-1's open interest. Some vendor feeds lag a further day (Alpaca: day-1 OI available on day 3), so check each record's open-interest date.
